items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: The name 'Bobby' appears only in the [INTERVIEWER] turn ('Bobby, did you ever live outside New Orleans...') as a form of address or reference to the interviewee. The interviewee does not mention a person named Bobby, nor does the text describe a relationship with anyone else named Bobby.

ctx.x: The boys in the band. But she's mother of them all. They'd get picked and stuff away around and all. I had a place up stage over the main floor. It was a pretty nice place. They had beds in there where these kids used to come there sometimes at night and sleep. Their mothers used to come to the house and ring up and wonder to find out where was your boy and all that sort of stuff. I'd have to tell them. They're here upstate sleeping or something else. They take the pillars, the feather pillars, and bust them open…

Bobby, did you ever live outside New Orleans or have you lived in New Orleans all your life? Do what? Have you lived in New Orleans all your life? Was I here all my life? Yeah. No. Where else did you live? I went to...

Some of my boys took a job up at St. Louis Fair. St. Louis Fair. That's in the 1890s. No, 1904. 1904. I see. Okay. They said for me to come up there. You understand? Uh-huh. And of course I had too many contracts down here, you know, to fill out. So I managed to spend a week up there with them. You understand? And they were playing out near the ground in an artificial palm garden. All artificial plants. Palm garden. Well, it seemed like there was three boys from, I don't know now, I forgot where they're from.…
